title: Topological Criticality with Charge-\(3e\) Fluctuations in the \(\mathrm{SU}(3)\) Triangular-Lattice Hofstadter--Hubbard Model
authors: Yang Liu, Ya-Hui Zhang, Xue-Yang Song
abstract: A transition between an integer quantum Hall insulator and a chiral spin liquid can become critical without closing the single-electron gap, raising the question of which composite excitations govern the change in topological order. We investigate this question in the \(\mathrm{SU}(3)\) triangular-lattice Hofstadter--Hubbard model at one particle per site and magnetic flux \(π/3\) per triangle. Using infinite density matrix renormalization group calculations, we identify a weak-coupling integer quantum Hall phase and an interaction-driven \(\mathrm{SU}(3)_1\) chiral spin liquid. Near the transition, both the neutral and charge-\(3e\) correlation lengths increase substantially, whereas the single-electron correlation length remains short, providing evidence for a Chern--Simons--Higgs critical theory, where a gauge-invariant monopole carries the quantum numbers of a fermionic \(\mathrm{SU}(3)\)-singlet trion. We discuss the implications for doping the system and recent experiments on doping \(ν=-2/3\) fractional quantum anomalous Hall in tMoTe\(_2\).
summary: This work investigates a topological phase transition in the SU(3) Hofstadter-Hubbard model, where the transition between an IQH state and a chiral spin liquid occurs without closing the single-electron gap. By analyzing correlation lengths, the authors provide evidence that the critical physics is governed by gauge-invariant, composite charge-3e excitations, supporting a Chern-Simons-Higgs critical theory.
main_problem: Investigating topological criticality in systems where the transition between distinct topological states occurs without closing the single-electron gap, suggesting the role of composite excitations.
main_result: The transition is governed by low-energy charge-3e fluctuations, consistent with a Chern-Simons-Higgs critical theory, evidenced by the divergence of the charge-3e correlation length while the single-electron length remains short.
method: Infinite Density Matrix Renormalization Group (iDMRG) calculations combined with parton mean-field theory and analysis of correlation lengths and entanglement spectra.
model_or_system: The study uses the SU(3) triangular-lattice Hofstadter-Hubbard Model, which incorporates hopping phases to generate a magnetic flux of pi/3 per triangle.
key_observables: Hall conductance (sigma_xy), neutral and charge-3e correlation lengths (xi_q), and entanglement spectra.
important_parameters: Interaction strength U, magnetic flux pi/3, and the filling factor (one particle per site).
main_assumptions: The single-electron gap remains open across the transition, and the analysis relies on interpreting the scaling behavior from finite bond dimensions.
figures_summary: Figures show diagnostics confirming the Integer Quantum Hall phase at weak coupling and the distinct enhancement of the charge-3e correlation length near the transition point.
paper_structure: The paper analyzes the system's topological response using iDMRG, identifies the relevant composite excitations (charge-3e monopole), and uses correlation length scaling to support a Chern-Simons-Higgs critical theory description.
why_interesting: The focus on fractionalized excitations (charge-3e) governing a topological phase transition, rather than single-electron excitations, provides a rich theoretical framework applicable to understanding exotic correlated materials.

figures.caption: FIG. 1: Diagnostics of the interaction-driven transition in the SU(3) Hofstadter–Hubbard model. At weak coupling, charge pumping is consistent with an IQH phase of Hall conductance 3e2/h. Near the transition, the pumped-charge response departs from its weak-coupling value. The chirality contributions resolved by local occupation sectors evolve as increasing repulsion favors single occupancy. These measurements are considered together with the entanglement spectrum and correlation lengths to identify the neighboring phases and transition region.

FIG. 2: Representation-resolved entanglement spectra in Real space of SU(3)1 CSL phase: (a) vacuum, (b) ¯3, and (c) 3 topological sectors. The low-lying levels are labeled by SU(3) representations. Their multiplet organization is compared with the corresponding SU(3)1 WZW conformal towers. The red box is for convenience of view only.

FIG. 3: Interaction dependence of the charge-3e and charge-e correlation lengths. Squares denote the charge-3e sector and triangles the charge-e sector. Where normalized values are shown, ξ0 is the value at the smallest U in the corresponding dataset. The charge-3e correlation length increases near the transition, whereas the single-electron correlation length shows no comparable enhancement.

FIG. 4: Correlation-length analysis near the candidate IQH–CSL transition. Top: interaction dependence of the inverse correlation lengths in (a) the neutral and (b) charge-3e sectors. Bottom: bond-dimension dependence for the corresponding sectors. The fits quantify the growth of correlation lengths and assess finite-entanglement effects. Extrapolation in bond dimension is performed at fixed cylinder circumference.

FIG. 5: Supplementary charge-3e correlation-length versus the interaction strength U for different cylinder circumferences and bond dimensions. The datasets include Ly = 4, 6, 7 at D = 8000 and Ly = 5, 6 at D = 7000.
